archetype.name: Lottery Team (shooting without the margins)
archetype.definition: A club that makes its shots at a near-elite rate but loses the possession game and can't get stops, leaving it well below water on both ends.

report.headline: The Clippers make shots; they just give away too many possessions to matter.
report.take:
Los Angeles is 4-11, 24th of 30 on the site, and the record is not a fluke. The Net Rtg of -6.5 ranks 23rd, the margin implies 5 wins rather than 4, and the W vs Pt Diff of -1 is a rounding error, not a hard-luck story. Carried over a full season, this is a 22-win pace. That is a sharp fall for a franchise that went 50-32 two years ago with the league's third-ranked defense and was still 42-40 last season.

The odd part is the offense. By shot-making alone this is a good team: 3P % of 38.7 ranks 2nd, TS % of 58.6 ranks 8th, and the 3PA Rate sits above the league average. Yet the ORtg of 111.6 is only 22nd. The leak is volume. TOV % of 15.6 is 29th, up from 13.2 last season, and ORB % of 24.6 is 25th, with RPG last in the league. The Clippers take fewer shots than their opponents, so their accuracy gets wasted. Darius Garland carries a 28.2 USG % with a 60.1 TS %, which looks fine until you see his On-Off of -20.8 and a backcourt graded D.

The defense is the deeper problem, and it has been sliding for two years. DRtg went from 110.3 in 2024-25 to 116.1 last season to 118.1 now, 25th. Opponents post a 56.5 Opp eFG % (28th), shoot 37.5% from three, get to the rim more than most (Opp Rim Rate 24th) and finish there at a below-average rate for the defense (22nd). Shooting guards fill the box score against them: the rebounds and assists they post rank 30th, and their PRA 28th. Brook Lopez is the one clear plus: a 64.8 TS %, the team's best BPM at 1.9, an On-Off of +9.4, and 16th of 92 on the centers tab. The lineups around him leak, though. Rui Hachimura (-10.3) and Isaiah Jackson (-11.4) both post deeply negative On-Off numbers.

November's offense was better than October's, 114 a game against 105.4, but the defense gave it right back, and the last three games were all double-digit losses. Some of the three-point shooting will cool, so the offense has no cushion to lose. Unless the turnovers and the glass come back toward last year's levels, this is a team settling into the lottery tier rather than one waiting for luck to turn.

strengths.title: Shot-making near the league's top
strengths.body: The Clippers rank 2nd in 3P % and 8th in TS %, about three points above the league from deep. It fits the franchise's history, which has hovered around 37-38% for years, though 38.7 is the high end of that band and likely cools somewhat. It is the only reason the offense isn't bottom-five.

strengths.title: Brook Lopez anchors the good minutes
strengths.body: Lopez scores efficiently, spaces the floor, and the team is far better with him on the court. He grades as the roster's best player by BPM, Win Shares and tab rank. The catch is that one positive center can't lift a frontcourt grade of C-, and the minutes without him get ugly.

strengths.title: Power forwards kept quiet
strengths.body: Opposing power forwards score less against the Clippers than almost anyone, and their share of the points against is well under the league's. Some of that is shape rather than skill: the damage simply shifts to the guards and centers.

concerns.title: A defense in a two-year slide
concerns.body: DRtg has gone from top-three in 2024-25 to 25th now, with opponents shooting well everywhere and getting to the rim too often. This is not one cold month. The trend runs across three seasons, and November's points allowed were worse than October's. Expect modest improvement at best.

concerns.title: Losing the possession game
concerns.body: A 29th-ranked TOV % and a 25th-ranked ORB % mean the efficient shooting arrives on too few shots. Turnovers are a new problem compared with last season. The rebounding weakness is older, since RPG was already low last year, so only the first looks fixable.

concerns.title: Garland's minutes bleed
concerns.body: Garland uses more possessions than anyone and scores fairly efficiently, but the team is dramatically worse with him on the floor. He sits mid-pack on the point guard tab, and the backcourt grades a D. With that much of the offense running through a negative-impact lead guard, the turnover and defensive numbers make sense.

trend.note: October and November produced nearly the same per-game margin: November's offense improved and its defense got worse by about as much. The last ten games sit right on the season line. Still, three straight double-digit losses close the stretch.

weekAhead.headline: Two road dates with the West's best, then a breather
weekAhead.body:
The week opens with back-to-back road trips to Houston and Memphis, two 12-5 teams ranked 1st and 5th on the site. Both attack exactly where the Clippers are weakest. Houston owns the league's best ORtg and second-best ORB %, against the league's worst rebounding team. Memphis pairs the top 3P % with the league's stingiest Opp 3P %, which takes away the Clippers' one reliable weapon.

The back half is kinder. New Orleans comes to LA with the league's 29th-ranked DRtg and lost 139-123 to the Clippers earlier this month. Golden State at home is a middling 9-8, but the Clippers lost there by 12 in the first meeting, and the Warriors force turnovers well. A split of the last two is realistic; anything better than 2-2 would be a surprise.

keyMatchups.title: Houston's glass against the league's worst
keyMatchups.body: Houston ranks 2nd in ORB % and 3rd in REB %, while the Clippers are last in RPG. Second chances could decide this one before the shooting does. Houston's defense also suppresses opposing centers, which limits Lopez as an outlet.

evidence.label: HOU C PRA vs avg rank

keyMatchups.title: Memphis shuts down the three
keyMatchups.body: Memphis allows the league's lowest Opp 3P %, and the Clippers' offense leans on being 2nd in 3P %. If the threes dry up, there is no rebounding or free-throw edge behind them. Memphis's wings grade an F, a small opening for Derrick Jones Jr.'s efficient scoring.

keyMatchups.title: New Orleans' open paint
keyMatchups.body: The Pelicans rank 29th in DRtg and Opp Rim FG %, and opposing power forwards and centers fill the box score against them. It is the week's best chance for Lopez and Hachimura, and the earlier 139-123 win shows the offense can feast here.

weekAhead.watch: Turnovers in Golden State: the Warriors rank 8th in forcing them, and that game is the likeliest swing between a 1-3 and a 2-2 week.

restOfSeason.body:
With 67 games left, the Clippers' margin matches their record, so there is no hidden bounce coming from close-game luck. The three-point shooting is the most likely number to slip, and the offense has little else to fall back on. The likeliest path forward is modest gains from cleaning up turnovers, which were far lower last season, partly cancelled by cooler shooting. The defense has eroded for two straight years and shouldn't be expected to snap back. That points to a finish in the low-to-high 20s in wins, a bit above the current pace if the turnover rate normalizes.

What would change the picture is the lineup balance. The team is clearly better with Lopez on the floor and worse with Garland, Hachimura and Jackson out there. A rotation that leans harder on its positive minutes could trim the margin toward -3, but nothing in the sheet suggests a playoff-caliber team hiding underneath.
swingFactors: Turnover rate returning toward last season's level
Whether the three-point shooting holds up
Lineups built around Lopez's positive minutes

confidence.note: 15 games is a small sample, but margin, record and multi-year defensive trend all agree.
